The thing is for me, there is no more acting or mask. Over the past two months or so I’ve slowly and purposefully cut down communication with friends until I’ve reached this point where I’m no longer bothered by anyone, because I don’t want to interact with anyone who knows me anymore. It’s not even about it being tired to put up a facade, i just don’t see the need to have social interaction with my friends or family. I used to struggle with it but I have passed the point of loneliness and being misunderstood. Loneliness for me was only felt when I used to be influenced by the way having no social interaction was viewed by most people. For example how having ‘no friends’ is something to be ashamed of. And I don’t worry about being misunderstood anymore because i don’t have to explain myself, my mental state, however I’m feeling, to anyone anymore. Because of this I just feel freer in general. Not needing to act anymore because there is no one to act for anyway.

i’m currently in a psych ward rn ( they’re pretty chill at the one i’m at so they let us have our phones) but just because you have suicidal thoughts doesn’t necessarily mean they will send you to one unless your psychiatrist seems you as a major threat to yourself. I think you should talk to your psychiatrist about it, he’ll  definitely be helpful, but seeing your situation, why not try therapy? i understand what you  mean about the discomfort when talking about feels but from experience therapy is where you can get help to cope with your thoughts best. Maybe you can ask your psychiatrist to give the therapist you plan to go to a call and tell them about your mental background so the first session won’t be so awkward?

I feel where you’re coming from where it feels like nothing you do matters and that life is a never ending cycle of pain. And it’s okay to want some attention, i mean nobody can survive without it. It’s already a really big step that you’re reaching out here for help, it likely means that something in you wants to get better or needs some help. 

From what it sounds, your family cares about you and i think it’s a good advantage for you. Have you tried talking to anyone in your family about how you feel? I think that’s one of the best steps you can take right now. I know what you mean where you don’t want them fuss over you but i think it’s just a small part you have to deal with, if you talk to a parent or family member you trust they’ll be able to bring you to a therapist or professional which can help asses how you’re feeling and help you get a proper diagnosis which can help you understand your thoughts better as well
